title: Maths reference: Year 7 Measurement
summary: The words and methods from Year 7 Measurement, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/measurement-7 (see snippets/maths-algebra-7.json for the format; split from the strand courses' card files on 1 Nov 2026).

items.label: scale
items.hint: A ratio of the drawing (or model) to the real thing. Each 1 unit on the drawing is 50 units in real life.

items.label: interior angle
items.hint: An angle inside a shape, at one of its corners.

items.label: polygon
items.hint: A closed shape with straight sides: triangle (3), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), octagon (8).

items.label: regular polygon
items.hint: All sides and all angles are equal, so each angle is the angle sum shared equally: a regular hexagon has angles of $120^\circ$.

items.label: perpendicular height
items.hint: The distance from the base to the opposite side or corner, at a right angle (∟) to the base. A slanted side is longer, and is not the height.

items.label: area of a parallelogram
items.hint: Cut the triangle off one end and move it: a rectangle with the same base and height.
items.board:

b: 6
h: 4
s: 2
cut: shown
units: cm
items.shows: A parallelogram cut and rearranged into a 6 by 4 rectangle

items.label: area of a triangle
items.hint: Two copies make a parallelogram with the same base and height; the triangle is half.
items.board:
widget: area
shape: triangle
b: 6
h: 4
s: 2
cut: shown
units: cm
items.shows: A triangle and its turned copy make a parallelogram

items.label: composite area
items.hint: Split the shape into rectangles and triangles and add the parts, or subtract a missing part from a bigger shape. Put every length in the same unit first.

items.label: square units
items.hint: Area counts squares: cm², m². A 1 m square is 100 cm by 100 cm.

items.label: volume of a prism
items.hint: Each layer is the base (the cross-section); the height counts the layers. For a box, $V = l \times w \times h$.
items.board:
widget: prism
l: 4
w: 3
h: 5
units: cm
items.shows: A 4 by 3 by 5 box in layers of 12 cubes

items.label: cross-section
items.hint: The shape that is the same all the way along a prism, like a slice of bread. A triangular prism's cross-section is a triangle: halve first.
items.board:
widget: prism
base: triangle
l: 4
w: 3
h: 5
units: cm
items.shows: A triangular prism, half of a 4 by 3 box, 5 layers high

items.label: capacity
items.hint: How much a container holds. A 10 cm cube holds 1 litre.

items.label: volume of a prism
items.code: V = A h \qquad h = V \div A
items.hint: The area of the end times the length, for any right prism. Divide to find a missing length.

items.label: radius and diameter
items.hint: The radius goes from the centre to the edge; the diameter right across through the centre. A chord joins any two points; the diameter is the longest.
items.shows: A circle with its centre, radius, diameter, a chord and the circumference

items.label: pi
items.hint: The circumference divided by the diameter: the same for every circle. 3.14 and 22/7 are approximations.
items.board:
widget: circle
r: 1.5
roll: shown
show: none
units: cm
items.shows: A circle rolled out flat: just over 3 diameters

items.label: circumference
items.hint: Use the diameter, or double the radius. Backwards: $d = C \div \pi$. Exact answers keep π: $10\pi$ cm.

items.label: transversal
items.hint: Parallel lines go the same way and never meet; arrows (>>) mark them. A transversal crosses both, making eight angles.

items.label: corresponding angles
items.hint: The same place at each crossing (an F shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: a, e
items.shows: a and e: the same place at each crossing, both 120°

items.label: alternate angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, f
items.shows: c and f: between the lines, opposite sides, both 60°

items.label: co-interior angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on the same side (a C shape). With parallel lines they add to $180^\circ$: they are not equal unless both are $90^\circ$.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, e
items.shows: c and e: between the lines, same side, 60° + 120° = 180°

items.label: vertically opposite angles
items.hint: Opposite each other at one crossing: always equal, parallel lines or not. Not one of the parallel-line pairs.

items.label: give a reason
items.hint: For each angle you find, name the rule: corresponding or alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$; angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.

items.label: angle sum of a triangle
items.hint: True for every triangle, whatever its shape or size: tear off the corners and they fill a straight line.

items.label: angle sum of a polygon
items.hint: Split it into triangles from one corner: a shape with $n$ sides makes $n - 2$ triangles. A pentagon: $3 \times 180^\circ = 540^\circ$.

sides: 5
corners: 2,1; 9,1; 10,5; 6,7; 1,5

items.shows: A pentagon splits into 3 triangles from A: 540°
